title: Combination Sum
statement:
List every distinct combination of numbers that adds up to a target, reusing numbers freely.

Contract
- `candidates` holds distinct positive integers and may be empty. `target` is positive.
- Return every combination of candidates whose sum is exactly `target`. A candidate may appear
  any number of times in a combination.
- Combinations are multisets: `[2, 3]` and `[3, 2]` are the same combination and must be reported
  once. Each reported combination must be unique.
- The order of the combinations and the order of the numbers inside each combination do not
  matter. Return an empty list when nothing reaches the target. Do not mutate `candidates`.

Examples
- `combinations(new int[]{2, 3, 6, 7}, 7)` returns `[[2, 2, 3], [7]]` in any order.
- `combinations(new int[]{2, 4}, 5)` returns `[]`.
- `combinations(new int[]{1, 2}, 3)` returns `[[1, 1, 1], [1, 2]]` in any order.
hints: Build a combination one number at a time and track how much of the target is still missing.
To avoid reporting the same multiset in different orders, only allow the next number to come from the current candidate or a later one. Stop a branch when the remainder reaches zero or goes negative.

Sort the candidates so a branch can stop as soon as one is too large. The number of results is exponential in general; the probe uses candidates {1, 2}, which gives about n/2 combinations of length up to n. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space for that family, where n is the target.
inputSyntax: Input: the candidates followed by the target, for example: [2, 3, 6, 7] 7
